## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The timestamp semantics and NULL documentation should be fixed because they misrepresent active processes and processes with prior starts.

## Changes
The pull request adds `finished_at` to the latest-event process model, documents the column, and adds `review.txt`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — Stop marking started processes as finished — For process 20, whose latest event is `started`, you expose its start timestamp as `finished_at`. The CASE selects `started`, while `models/schema.yml:11` defines the column as the time the process finished. — Consumers using a non-null finish timestamp to identify completed processes will classify this active process as completed. — Fix: Select the completion event, or rename and document the column if a start timestamp is intended.
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Correct the documented meaning of NULL — For process 30 (`started` then `cleared`), your model returns NULL despite a recorded start. “NULL means the process has never been started” contradicts `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end` applied only to `recency = 1`. — Consumers following this catalog entry will mistake previously started processes for processes that have never started.
